title: Localization commutes with tensor products
statement: Let $S\subseteq R$ be a multiplicative subset of a commutative ring $R$. An $R$-linear map $\ell:P\to P'$ of $R$-modules is a *localization of $P$ at $S$* if (a) every $s\in S$ acts bijectively on $P'$, (b) every element of $P'$ is $s^{-1}\ell(p)$ for some $p\in P$, $s\in S$, and (c) $\ell(p)=\ell(q)$ implies $sp=sq$ for some $s\in S$ (equivalently, (a) holds and $S^{-1}P\to P'$, $p/s\mapsto s^{-1}\ell(p)$, is bijective). Let $A$ be an $R$-algebra whose structure map $R\to A$ is a localization of $R$ at $S$, let $M,N$ be $R$-modules and $M',N'$ $A$-modules (regarded as $R$-modules via $R\to A$), and let $\ell_M:M\to M'$, $\ell_N:N\to N'$ be $R$-linear maps that are localizations at $S$. Then the $R$-linear map $\ell:M\otimes_RN\to M'\otimes_AN'$, $m\otimes n\mapsto\ell_M(m)\otimes\ell_N(n)$, is a localization of $M\otimes_RN$ at $S$. In particular $S^{-1}M\otimes_{S^{-1}R}S^{-1}N\cong S^{-1}(M\otimes_RN)$, $(m/s)\otimes(n/t)\mapsto(m\otimes n)/st$.
